name: Aspartame
description: Aspartame is a low-calorie artificial sweetener, approximately 200 times sweeter than sucrose (table sugar). It is widely used in sugar-free products like diet sodas, chewing gum, and gelatin. Aspartame is composed of two amino acids: aspartic acid and phenylalanine.
scientific_consensus: The FDA and EFSA have deemed aspartame safe for the general population at current levels of consumption. However, it must be avoided by individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU), a rare genetic disorder that prevents the metabolism of phenylalanine.

name: Red 40 (Allura Red AC)
description: Red 40 is a petroleum-based azo dye used to color foods and beverages red. It is one of the most widely used food dyes in the US.
scientific_consensus: Approved by the FDA for use in food. However, some studies suggest a link between artificial food dyes and hyperactivity (ADHD symptoms) in sensitive children. The EU requires a warning label on products containing Red 40.

name: High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS)
description: HFCS is a sweetener made from corn starch that has been processed to convert some of its glucose into fructose. It is chemically similar to table sugar (sucrose) but cheaper to produce.
scientific_consensus: Nutritionally equivalent to table sugar, but its ubiquity in processed foods contributes to excessive calorie intake, obesity, and metabolic syndrome. Excessive fructose consumption can strain the liver.

name: Sodium Benzoate
description: Sodium benzoate is a preservative used to prevent the growth of bacteria and mold in acidic foods like soda, jams, and pickles.
scientific_consensus: Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA. However, when combined with Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) under heat/light, it can form benzene, a known carcinogen. Levels are strictly regulated.

name: Titanium Dioxide (E171)
description: Used to make foods look whiter or more opaque. Common in candies, chewing gum, and pastries.
scientific_consensus: The FDA considers it safe. However, the EFSA (European Food Safety Authority) banned it as a food additive in 2022 due to concerns that nanoparticles could damage DNA (genotoxicity).

name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
description: MSG is a sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid found naturally in many foods like tomatoes and cheese. It enhances savory (umami) flavor.
scientific_consensus: Extensive research shows MSG is safe for most people. 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' (headache, numbness) has been largely debunked as a myth or placebo effect in controlled studies, though a small percentage of people may have mild sensitivity.

name: Carrageenan
description: Derived from red seaweed, used to thicken and stabilize foods like soy milk, ice cream, and deli meats.
scientific_consensus: Food-grade carrageenan is safe. However, 'degraded' carrageenan (poligeenan) causes inflammation and is not allowed in food. Some animal studies suggest food-grade carrageenan might still cause gut inflammation in sensitive individuals.
